paragraphs.source_en: The Round Head complex is dominated by anthropomorphic figures. Sansoni (1994: 204) estimates that they represent 73% of all images, followed by 25. 6% of zoomorphic figures and 0. 6% of objects and signs. Of the anthropomorphic figures, 49. 3% are represented by male and 10. 2% by female figures, the rest being unidentifiable. Not only are the male figures four times more numerous than the female ones but they are also aesthetically different. Males are represented more frequently with body decoration, body adornments and masks. In compositions, men and women are either mixed together or separated according to sex.

paragraphs.source_en: Images that only appear in particular areas include round bracelets, objects in an inverted T-shaped form which are attached on a male figures' back, and half-moon like objects attached on figures' shoulders or painted as isolated objects. The least represented amongst the characteristic elements is a so-called Great God, a large male figure with raised hands, in a dominant position and often with smaller figures around it, apparently in worship (Fig. 3-2; 3-3; 3-4).
